actual_disposition: In a preliminary ruling, the Court held that consent is not validly constituted by a pre-checked checkbox that the user must deselect; that the interpretation does not differ according to whether the stored or accessed information is personal data; and that clear and comprehensive information includes cookie duration and whether third parties may access the cookies.

principal_findings.finding: Article 2(f) and Article 5(3) of Directive 2002/58/EC, read with Directive 95/46/EC Article 2(h) and GDPR Articles 4(11) and 6(1)(a), require active consent; a pre-checked checkbox that must be deselected is insufficient.
The Article 5(3) protection applies to storing or accessing information in terminal equipment regardless of whether that information is personal data.
Clear and comprehensive information under Article 5(3) includes the duration of cookie operation and whether third parties may access the cookies.
Directive 95/46/EC governed the earlier period, while GDPR applicability to the forward-looking injunction was for the referring court to ascertain; the CJEU answered with regard to both regimes.

important_qualifications: The Court did not determine whether making advertising consent a condition of lottery participation was compatible with the requirement that consent be freely given, because that question was not referred.
The preliminary ruling interpreted EU law; application to the national dispute and costs remained for the national court.
The information ruling concerned circumstances such as those in the main proceedings and did not purport to exhaust every disclosure duty for every cookie use.
